entries.title: Bulls' offense won't change without Caleb Wilson
entries.summary: <p>With one win in the Bulls’ first 10 games, fans were coming to grips with the idea that this season would be about Caleb Wilson’s development and his pursuit of the NBA Rookie of the Year award.</p><p>Both are on hold after Wilson, the fourth overall pick in the draft, had surgery Thursday for a broken right hand he suffered Wednesday against the Spurs. For at least a month, fans will have to put their focus on something else — and that won’t be easy on this team.</p><p>Wilson entered the game Friday against the Hawks as the Bulls’ second-leading scorer, averaging 18.9 points, just behind team leader Norman Powell (19.3). Among rookies, Wilson was third in scoring, first in steals per game (1.8) and second in blocked shots (0.9). He was among the early leaders for the top rookie honor.</p><p>“To see a guy that’s just come in, he’s played 10 games in the NBA, he’s playing really well and then to get injured like that, it sucks,” Josh Giddey said.</p><p>“He’s frustrated, just like all of us,” coach Tiago Splitter said.</p><p>Wilson has been unlucky with his hand health. At North Carolina, he broke his left hand in February, and after being cleared to work out, he broke his right thumb on a dunk in March. It’s widely believed that had Wilson not gotten hurt, he wouldn’t have fallen to the Bulls.</p><p>That’s one break that went the Bulls’ way. Splitter said he asked Wilson about his rash of hand injuries.</p><p>“It’s just bad luck, a freak injury,” Splitter said. “Just have to be patient.”</p><p>The Bulls hadn’t been so patient on the court with Wilson. They had been throwing a lot at him, and he had been responding with not just numbers but development. He also had been jelling with his teammates in Splitter’s uptempo offense.</p><p>Now that offense, which finally has been working as it's supposed to — better shooting certainly has helped — is without a key cog. But Splitter said he won’t change the offense, though others will have to make up for the team-high 16 shots Wilson took per game.</p><p>“Of course, we’re going to miss him, but it doesn’t change what we want to do,” Splitter said. “Everybody else is going to have more shots. I don’t expect just one guy to be more aggressive. Naturally, the game’s going to find the shots, and the players are going to take those shots. I’m not worried about that.”</p><p>“It’s a big hole to fill,” Giddey said. “He was very productive for us on both sides of the ball. I don’t think it’s as simple as just putting someone in to replace Caleb. It’s going to have to be by committee. It allows opportunities for other guys to come in and play a bigger role.”</p><p>Two of those players will be big men Nic Claxton and Jalen Smith, who Splitter said will see more time together now that Claxton is closer to playing normal minutes. He was restricted to about 16-20 minutes in his first two games back from a hamstring injury that cost him a month. Splitter said the team wants him to play about 20-24 minutes.</p><p>Fortunately for the Bulls, Powell returned from back spasms that kept him out of two games. The veteran guard entered the game averaging the second-most shots on the team with 13, though he had made only 40% of them, 70 points below his career average.</p><p>As for Wilson, Splitter said he’ll stay involved with the team, being at practice and watching video. Splitter said that was important for Wilson, as well as seeing the game from a different perspective. With a hand injury, he’ll be able to stay in shape, though not exactly game shape. Splitter had an idea interesting idea for Wilson.</p><p>“Maybe work on the left hook or something like that,” he said.</p>

entries.title: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop. O'Hare, Midway flights can resume after hours of delays, cancellations
entries.summary: <p>Hours after the Federal Aviation Administration halted flights across the country Friday, including at Midway and O'Hare airports, the agency said departures can resume.</p><p>Officials blamed “an incredibly old air traffic control system" for instability in air traffic control communications during a White House briefing Friday evening.</p><p>Inside O’Hare International Airport — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2026/01/20/ohare-reclaims-top-spot-named-nations-busiest-airport-in-2025" target="_blank" >the busiest airport in the U.S.</a> — confused passengers wandered around as luggage piled up on baggage carousels. Long lines of travelers rummaged through hundreds of bags from flights that never took off because of the delay.</p><p>The FAA grounded all flights nationwide at around 2:36 p.m., and an FAA alert said the stoppage was "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety." They said they lifted the ground stop at 7:15 p.m., though it was unclear when flights actually would resume.</p><p>A sudden silence fell over O'Hare as travelers were notified that the ground stop had been lifted. But a video board displaying flight information still showed delays or cancellations even though many passengers attempted to buy tickets at nearby airline kiosks. </p><p>"For an 18-hour trip back and forth, it doesn't make sense for us and try to go," said Angelica Colmenares, who was en route to Paris for a 48-hour trip with a friend. Luckily, we were flying standby so we didn't fly, but now we're going to have our own party in Chicago."</p><p>Some airlines, including JetBlue and Air Canada, had already said they were canceling the rest of their Friday night flights.</p><p>U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said the public was "never in danger" and the flights were grounded due to an "abundance of caution."</p><p>By 5:30 p.m., O'Hare had reported 328 flight cancellations and 847 delays. Midway saw 30 canceled flights and 186 delays, according to the <a class="Link" href="https://www.flychicago.com/business/media/delays/pages/default.aspx" target="_blank" >Chicago Department of Aviation</a>. </p><p>As of 6:15 p.m. on Friday, 30 flights scheduled to arrive at O'Hare since 2:55 p.m. had been diverted. Ten arrivals scheduled at Midway were also diverted. </p><p>U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue affected all of the nation's 22 air traffic control centers that route planes between airports.</p><p>During the evening briefing, Duffy shifted focus to a political fight, saying the Trump administration had been “asking Congress to fully fund a full build of a brand new air traffic control system.”</p><p>Mullin said there was no sign yet that "this was a nefarious attack against us. It's just a telecommunications outage."</p><p>“Everybody's safe. There's no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they're flying,” he said.</p><p>Although the order was lifted, Duffy said he expected it to take a bit to catch up on flight schedules. “Hopefully tomorrow, we are going to start to see far better movement,” he said.</p><p>Earlier at O'Hare, video boards displaying flight information were checkered with red and yellow, signifying the delays and cancellations that forced many travelers to book hotel rooms for the night or rent a car to arrive at their destinations.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div across the country. </p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Tyler Pasciak LaRiviere/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Prospect Heights residents Matt and Patricia Kowalski arrived at O’Hare two hours early for their annual holiday trip to visit family in Poland, prepared to board a flight to Germany.</p><p>Matt Kowalski learned through the radio on their ride to the airport that a ground stop had occurred, so they decided to wait it out.</p><p>By 5 p.m., they had already missed their connecting flight and were debating waiting another three investigators will look at whether there is any link to the FAA's nationwide rollout of a new artificial intelligence system to help identify problems and reroute planes. But that system operates out of one location near Washington, D.C., and just sends recommendations to the air traffic control centers.</p><p>The FAA, in a separate statement, said the ground stop was issued "out of an abundance of caution. "Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case-by-case basis," the FAA said.</p><p>Nashville resident Paul Lindsay, who was at O'Hare, was on his way to Mason City, Iowa, with friends.</p><p>"This is nuts," he said. "It's good to know this is not our problem. Every person in an airport in the United States is running into this problem."</p><p>The Chicago Department of Aviation said it had no comment and directed questions to the FAA.</p><p>U.S. Rep. Jesús “Chuy” García, D-Ill., a member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, called for more congressional oversight of the FAA and air traffic control in a statement Friday evening.</p><p>“My team and I are monitoring the nationwide ground stop that the FAA has ordered, which is causing major travel disruptions and affecting millions nationwide," the statement said. "... I will demand answers from the FAA; Congress must be briefed, and there must be a thorough investigation into the cause of this massive disruption to our aviation system.”</p><div class="Enhancement" Check back for updates.</i></p><p><i>Contributing: Associated Press</i></p>

entries.title: CPS faces possible midyear budget cuts as unexpected funding costs mount
entries.summary: <p>Just a few months into the school year, Chicago Public Schools has overspent its budget and its emergency contingency budget for special education by $27 million — one of several “compounding financial pressures” that could mean midyear cuts if the school district doesn’t get more from the state in the state Legislative veto session that starts Tuesday.</p><p>Besides ballooning special education costs, CPS officials say they had to pay more than expected in interest on short-term loans to make payroll and received $19 million less in state funding than expected.</p><p>And these unexpected costs don’t even include the staff that CPS rehired this fall at the direction of school board members aligned with the Chicago Teachers Union. In a controversial move, these members approved a last-minute budget amendment counting on $150 million more from the state, even though it had yet to be committed.</p><p>The district only wound up re-hiring some of the staff laid off — 128 teachers and 153 support staff at a cost of $29 million. District officials are already planning to re-lay off those staff members as early as Dec. 1 if no additional money comes through, according to a memo obtained by the Chicago Tribune.</p><p>But district officials have yet to say how they plan to handle the other costs that are creating a hole in the district’s budget.</p><p>“The CPS Finance team is closely monitoring our budget, assessing implications of rising costs and a shortfall if no additional state revenue is received, and identifying potential solutions,” CPS officials said in a statement. “CPS will continue to keep our Board and community apprised of any additional financial savings that will need to be enacted this school year.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> In 2017, Illinois changed the way it distributed funds to school districts. The law established the amount of funding each district needs to provide an adequate education. Illinois has fallen way behind on meeting those targets.</p><p>Of about 940 school districts, 714 have moved further away from adequacy this school year. That’s despite education funding in Illinois rising overall under Pritzker. In Chicago, CPS now has only 70% of what it needs to provide an adequate education, down from 73% last year and 79% the year before.</p><p>Many factors are causing the state to fall short, including a change in the way the state counts the number of poor students and costs going up.</p><p>Any state funding package would likely need to include much more than what CPS needs and money for other underfunded districts in order to get any traction, making it a costly proposition. entries.title: Bulls get long-awaited second victory in first game without Caleb Wilson
entries.summary: <p>It looked as though the Bulls were going to let another big lead get away when their 18-point edge over the Hawks disappeared. But they kept it together, and <b>Norman Powell</b> took over by scoring nine of his 33 points in overtime to lead them to a 125-117 victory for their long-awaited second triumph of the season.</p><p>For a team that entered the day on an eight-game skid, the Bulls (2-9) showed a lot of fight during the game and a lot of emotion as it ended.</p><p>‘‘It’s not easy to lose a lot of games,’’ coach <b>Tiago Splitter</b> said. ‘‘You’ve got to stay composed; you’ve got to stay locked in. But that frustration’s still there. And when you win a game, sometimes that stuff comes out.’’</p><p><b>Josh Giddey</b> had his first triple-double of the season with 15 points, 10 rebounds and 14 assists. The Bulls had 34 assists for the game — evidence of the way Splitter wants to play, with or without rookie <b>Caleb Wilson</b>, who missed his first of many games with a broken right hand.</p><p>The Bulls got plenty of contributions, with seven players scoring in double figures. <b>Isaac Okoro</b> and <b>Jalen Smith</b> also scored 15 points, <b>Patrick Williams</b> had 13, <b>Buddy Hield</b> 12 and <b>Matas Buzelis</b> 11, including a big three-pointer with 23.5 seconds left in overtime that gave the Bulls a six-point lead.</p><p>And for those interested, the Bulls put themselves in the running for at least a wild-card spot in the NBA Cup. The victory put them in a three-way tie for second with the Wizards and Hawks in East Group C at 1-1. With winnable remaining games against the Wizards and Hornets, a 3-1 record is possible.</p><h3>Robinson fills out roster</h3><p>The Bulls signed center <b>Orlando Robinson</b> from their G League affiliate, Windy City, to fill their 15th and final standard-contract roster spot. With a full roster, the Bulls’ two-way players — <b>Tobe Awaka</b>, <b>Jordan Hawkins</b> and <b>Jaylin Sellers</b>, who split time with Windy City — are eligible to play in 50 games each, rather than 90 combined.</p><p>Splitter said Robinson earned the spot. He averaged 13.7 points and eight rebounds in three games for Windy City. He also played in three preseason games for the Bulls, averaging 6.3 points and 4.3 rebounds. The 26-year-old has appeared in 115 NBA games in four seasons, playing for the Heat, Kings, Raptors and Magic.</p><p>‘‘Orlando was great for us in camp,’’ Splitter said. ‘‘He’s a great spirit on the bench, always good vibes. Our guys love him. It’s a reward from the camp that he had for us.’’</p><h3>Still a happy place</h3><p>Despite all the Bulls’ losing, Giddey said he and his teammates still enjoy coming to work and are putting in the effort to improve.</p><p>‘‘Clearly, we’re not up to where we should be,’’ he said. ‘‘Teams are showing us that, and we’ve got to be able to put 48 minutes together. But the group’s positive, the building’s positive. It’s a place I love to come in every day and see everybody and work. We all have the same goal of getting back to winning games.’’</p><p>If they don’t, the season might be historically bad. The Bulls are on pace to win 15 games, which would equal the franchise low for a full season, set in 2000-01. The Bulls won 13 games in the lockout-shortened 1988-89 season.</p><h3>Historic achievement</h3><p>Big men <b>Nic Claxton</b> and <b>Jalen Smith</b> each had at least 17 points and an 83.3 field-goal percentage Wednesday against the Spurs. It was the first time in team history two centers put up those numbers in the same game. Smith had 23 points and shot 88.9%.</p>

entries.title: New Trier's Throy Nightingale runs for 5 TDs, 309 yards in emotional state quarterfinal win against Huntley
entries.summary: <p>New Trier’s football team learned that classmate Brock Beeler had died as they took the field to practice on Wednesday.</p><p>“It is hard watching 17- and 18-year-olds find that news out,” Trevians coach Brian Doll said. “We just needed to be there for them. Football is football, but life is life. We needed to do something for our kids that day and support them. I canceled practice right when I found out. It was a tough decision but the right decision.”</p><p>“It was the right move,” New Trier senior Harry Resis said. “A lot of our captains were really close with Brock, and we needed some time to reset and think about what happened. And just grieve together.”</p><p>Beeler played football his sophomore year, and his jersey hung on the sideline on Friday night in Huntley as the Trevians beat the Red Raiders 42-28 in a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2026/10/17/ihsa-state-football-playoff-pairings-class8a-illinois-2026" >Class 8A</a> quarterfinal.</p><p>“It just means a lot that we can get a win in his honor and bring everyone together and make the community feel a little better in a time of sadness and loss,” Resis said.</p><p>Resis, a tight end, and linemen Nicholas Danielsen and Sean Feeney were part of a New Trier rushing attack that overwhelmed undefeated Huntley (11-1).</p><p>Senior running back Throy Nightingale Jr. carried the load, rushing 39 times. He finished with a career-high 309 yards and scored five touchdowns.</p><p>“It’s a great feeling getting support [from the line],” Nightingale said. “It was amazing getting support from them. They said to keep going, and I kept going.”</p><p>Nightingale transferred to New Trier from Notre Dame this year, but still knew Beeler.</p><p>“It was definitely tough,” Nightingale said. “[Beeler] would be here right now, and I know he would want us to keep going and to keep pushing. So we did that for him tonight.”</p><p>The Trevians (11-1) led 21-0 in the second quarter after Nightingale’s second TD run.</p><p>Huntley pulled within 21-14 early in the second half on a 10-yard touchdown pass from Malik Carter to Matthew Schroeder. But that was as close as it would get.</p><p>“[New Trier] took it to us today in all three phases, really,” Red Raiders coach Mike Naymola said. “They were a lot more physical than us. I was proud of what these guys were able to do. We were resilient and fought back, and right when we got ourselves back in the game they made another play.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> entries.title: No. 3 Illini get back to winning ways vs. Sam Houston
entries.summary: <p>Tomislav Ivisic had a career-high 28 points, Andrej Stojakovic added 26 and No. 3 Illinois bounced back from its first loss this season with a 108-86 victory over Sam Houston on Friday night in Champaign.</p><p>Coming off an 84-78 defeat Tuesday night at No. 16 Texas Tech, the Fighting Illini (3-1) pulled away from the Bearkats by scoring 63 points in the second half to set up a high-profile showdown with No. 2 Duke next week.</p><p>After trailing 45-40 at halftime, Sam Houston (2-2) went in front 57-56 with 15:58 left on a fast-break dunk by Enel St. Bernard. Ivisic answered 14 seconds later with a 3-pointer that launched an 11-0 run for the Illini, who never trailed again.</p><p>Ivisic scored 10 of the first 14 points for Illinois in the second half. He briefly left the court midway through the period after being elbowed in the mouth, but returned and finished the game.</p><p>Stefan Vaaks scored 14 points off the bench, and Quentin Coleman had 11 points, eight rebounds and six assists for Illinois. Ethan Brown also scored 11.</p><p>Justin Begg had 19 points and 10 assists for the Bearkats. Aidan McDowell also scored 19 points, Yoda Oke added 14 off the bench and Jacobe Coleman finished with 11.</p><p>The Illini forced 14 turnovers, converting them into 19 points, and had nine steals and six blocks.</p><p>Illinois is 3-0 at home and has scored at least 108 points in all three blowouts.</p><p>It was the first game between Illinois and Sam Houston, but Illini coach Brad Underwood improved to 9-0 against the Bearkats. The first eight wins came in the Southland Conference from 2013-16 when Underwood was the coach at Stephen F. Austin.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>Sam Houston visits Wyoming on Tuesday.</p><p>Illinois plays at No. 2 Duke on Tuesday.</p><p></p><p><b>DePAUL 67, NORTHWESTERN 47</b></p><p>Kruz McClure scored 18 points and Koree Cotton added 15 as DePaul defeated crosstown foe Northwestern 67-47 on Friday night.</p><p>The Blue Demons (4-0) took down the Wildcats (3-1) for the first time since Dec. 21, 2019, and the first time in Evanston since Dec. 27, 2013. Northwestern had not trailed at any point in three previous games.</p><p>DePaul shot just 36% as a team and 31% from deep, but held Northwestern to 31% and 25% marks. The Blue Demons hit 11 3-pointers, their third straight game in double-figures.</p><p>Fabian Flores grabbed eight rebounds, and Cotton and Magoon Gwath each had six. Layden Blocker had two blocks and two steals.</p><p>The two teams traded the lead back-and-forth in a low-scoring first half, and DePaul led 27-23 at the break. Cotton and McClure each had eight points in the first.</p><p>The Blue Demons opened the second half with consecutive 3-pointers by Popoola and Cotton, stretching their advantage to double-digits. They went on runs of 6-0 and 7-0 to cruise to a comfortable victory.</p><p>Jake West scored a game-high 20 for the Wildcats and LA Pratt had 10. West has reached 20 points in all four games this season.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>DePaul: hosts Maryland Eastern on Tuesday.</p><p>Northwestern: hosts Columbia on Monday.</p>
